hints: Focus on what the Finkelstein reaction does not do, it only swaps the halogen in place with no change to the carbon skeleton.
Decode compound X from its skeletal formula as $\text{(CH}_3\text{)}_2\text{CHCH}_2\text{CH(CH}_3\text{)CH}_2\text{I}$, a primary iodoalkane with methyl branches at two positions.
Look for the option with the exact same carbon backbone but with $\text{Cl}$ or $\text{Br}$ on the same primary carbon where $\text{I}$ is now.
walkthrough:
**Recall what Finkelstein does**

Think of this as a simple swap. The C-Cl or C-Br bond becomes C-I, nothing else moves.

$$\text{R-CH}_2\text{-Cl + I}^- \rightarrow \text{R-CH}_2\text{-I + Cl}^-$$
The question also tells you it only works for primary halogenoalkanes, so the $\text{-CH}_2\text{Cl}$ or $\text{-CH}_2\text{Br}$ group must be attached to only one other carbon.

**Decode the skeleton of X**

Read the skeletal drawing from left to right. The fork on the left is $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CH-}$, then $-\text{CH}_2-$, then $-\text{CH(CH}_3)-$, then $-\text{CH}_2\text{I}$.

$$\text{X = (CH}_3\text{)}_2\text{CHCH}_2\text{CH(CH}_3\text{)CH}_2\text{I}$$
This is 1-iodo-2,4-dimethylpentane. The $\text{CH}_2\text{I}$ carbon is primary, and the backbone has 5 carbons in the longest chain with methyls on C2 and C4.

**Match the precursor**

The starting material must have the identical backbone $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CHCH}_2\text{CH(CH}_3\text{)CH}_2-$ with $\text{Cl}$ or $\text{Br}$ in place of $\text{I}$, and that halogen must also be primary.
Only $\text{(CH}_3\text{)}_2\text{CHCH}_2\text{CH(CH}_3\text{)CH}_2\text{Cl}$ fits both tests perfectly, giving X by direct substitution.

options.A: Backbone is wrong. This is $\text{(CH}_3\text{)}_2\text{CHCH(CH}_3\text{)CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{Br}$, which would give $\text{(CH}_3\text{)}_2\text{CHCH(CH}_3\text{)CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{I}$. That has methyl branches on adjacent carbons (3,4-dimethyl pattern), not the 2,4-dimethyl pattern of X. It is primary, so it would react, but it makes the wrong isomer.
options.B: Chain is too short. This is $\text{(CH}_3\text{)}_2\text{CHCH(CH}_3\text{)CH}_2\text{Br}$, only 4 carbons in the main chain. Its product would be $\text{(CH}_3\text{)}_2\text{CHCH(CH}_3\text{)CH}_2\text{I}$, which is missing one $\text{CH}_2$ group compared to X.
options.C: Two errors. The skeleton is $\text{(CH}_3\text{)}_2\text{CHCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH(CH}_3\text{)Cl}$, a 6-carbon chain, not the 5-carbon chain of X. More importantly, the $\text{Cl}$ is on a $\text{CH(CH}_3\text{)Cl}$ carbon, which is secondary. The question states the reaction only works for primary halogenoalkanes, so this would not react.
options.D: Perfect match. This is $\text{(CH}_3\text{)}_2\text{CHCH}_2\text{CH(CH}_3\text{)CH}_2\text{Cl}$ with the same 2,4-dimethylpentane backbone as X. The $\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}$ group is primary, so Finkelstein substitution works, and direct replacement of $\text{Cl}$ by $\text{I}$ gives exactly X.
